title: PMIC reset <-> driver-hang correlation: nightshift diary + mitigation proposals
content:
Context and motivation:

This is a nightshift grok-and-propose note capturing a cluster of driver-hang incidents over 48h where nodes showed transient PMIC (power-management IC) resets around the same time as long-running GPU driver soft-hangs (processes stuck, no progress, no hard kernel panic). Pattern surfaced after a ramp in training jobs using sustained high-power kernels. High-level goal: codify observable signals, immediate mitigations, and an initial runbook for oncall to reduce blast radius until hardware/vendor follow-up is complete.

Summary of observed incidents (high-level):
- Window: 2029-10-30 22:40 -> 2029-11-01 03:15 UTC.
- Affected nodes: ~7 unique hosts across 3 racks; all commercial A100-similar cards (same vendor batch).
- Symptoms: one or more GPUs on the host stop responding to user-level health probes (nvml reports TIMEOUT / stale responses). No immediate kernel oops. dmesg shows i2c/PMIC reset lines and a short burst of NVLink retraining attempts. Driver (nvidia) _softly_ blocked: processes using libcuda hang waiting on RPCs, but the host remains reachable via SSH.
- Recovery: most nodes recovered after 5–12 minutes (either automatic GPU reboot by firmware or full host reboot triggered manually). Two nodes required manual power-cycle (OOB) to clear.

Why this feels different from past ECC-only waves:
- ECC logs (correctable) were present but not dominant. The stronger signal was PMIC/VRM glitching and a correlated fan-speed oscillation.
- NVLink retraining attempts happened *after* PMIC messages, which suggests power-plane disturbance precedes link errors.
- No immediate kernel panic or persistent driver oops; these look like soft-hangs that sometimes self-heal.

Detailed timeline (compiled from logs / timestamps):
- 2029-10-30T22:41:12Z host-12: nv-power: PMIC event: pwr_seq_unstable event_id=0x2a3
- 2029-10-30T22:41:13Z host-12: nvidia: nvlink: link retrain start slot=1
- 2029-10-30T22:41:14Z host-12: nvidia: nvml: device 0 timeout while responding to health check
- 2029-10-30T22:41:20Z host-12: kubelet: eviction controller attempted to drain pod gpu-train-11 (blocked)
- 2029-10-30T22:46:30Z host-12: fw: gpu watchdog reset (firmware triggered)
- 2029-10-30T23:02:05Z host-07: similar PMIC event; nvlink retrain; driver soft hang; automatic recovery at 23:07 after firmware reset.

Immediate hypotheses (ranked):
1) PMIC/VRM transient voltage sag due to sustained high-power kernels + fan control oscillations -> causes temporary loss of power rails on GPU PCIe domain -> firmware triggers local GPU reset -> driver hangs until reset completes.
2) A faulty PMIC on a subset of PSUs that trips under cyclic load, producing ripple; NVLink hardware sees link loss and triggers retrain; driver goes into a blocking state while NVML operations time out.
3) A driver bug where NVML health probe does not handle transient power sequencing gracefully and ends up blocking thread pool (worse under high load), so symptoms look like driver soft-hang rather than immediate kernel panic.
4) BIOS / platform microcode interacting badly with GPU PMIC resets resulting in host-level PCIe device state confusion (requires vendor firmware analysis).

Telemetry to check (quick checklist for oncall):
- ssh to host -> journalctl -u nvidia-driver (or /var/log/nvidia) around timestamp. Look for "PMIC" or "pwr_seq" entries.
- dmesg | tail -n 200 -> scan for i2c PMIC lines, PCIe reset, BAR0 unmap, or nvlink/training messages.
- nvml health probe: run nvmlDeviceGetAllClockInfo / nvidia-smi --query to see if device reports busy or timeout.
- ipmitool sel elist / ipmi SEL logs for PSU warnings around time.
- rack-level BMC logs: fan speeds reported; look for synchronous spikes across GPUs in same host.
- Prometheus panels: "gpu.power.draw", "gpu.fan.speed", "gpu.core_temp", "pcie.link.retrain_total" for the host/rack windows.
- Correlate with job scheduler: which workloads were running? (high sustained SM utilization math kernels vs mixed workloads).

Interim operational controls (low-risk, quick):
- Throttle long-running synthetic kernels via quota/soft-limits in job scheduler: enforce 5–10% headroom on sustained power draw if possible. Useful in high-risk racks.
- Add an automatic circuit: when we see PMIC event + nvml timeout on a GPU, mark node as "softquarantine" (taint the k8s node with reason=pmic-reset) and attempt automated firmware-triggered reboot (ipmitool chassis power cycle). If automatic reboot fails after N attempts, escalate to oncall for manual OOB power-cycle.
- Rapid roll: add a temporary policy to prefer dispatching ephemeral training jobs to other racks for 24–48h while we monitor.
- Enable more aggressive driver health probes (reduce timeout) so stuck processes are detected earlier and kubelet can evict pods/fallback. Tradeoff: possible false positives; adjust carefully.

Proposed runbook (first draft) - steps for oncall
1) Detect: alert triggers when (nvml_timeout > 3 for any GPU) OR (pmic_event_count > 0 and nvlink_retrain_count > 2) on a single host within 5m.
2) Triage: ssh to host-XX, capture dmesg (dmesg -T | sed -n '1,200p'), journalctl -u nvidia-driver --since "15 minutes ago". Copy logs to /tmp and to central log bucket.
3) Quarantine: taint node -> kubectl taint nodes host-XX gpu-pmic=quarantine:NoSchedule; annotate with incident id.
4) Attempt soft-recover: trigger nvidia-firmware-refresh script (internal tool) which attempts a driver unload and firmware reset. Command: sudo /usr/local/bin/nvidia-firmware-refresh --device=all --verbose (note: might not be safe under kernel lockups; see special-cases below).
5) If driver-refresh succeeds and devices return healthy within 5m, untaint and monitor for 2h.
6) If no recovery or driver unload blocks: initiate controlled host reboot via ipmitool chassis bootdev pxe; ipmitool chassis power cycle. If IPMI fails, escalate to OOB team to power-cycle via pdus.
7) Post-recovery: collect full PMIC logs, nvlink status, and power telemetry; file ticket to vendors and schedule batch firmware update tests.
8) Notify scheduling team to avoid sensitive workloads on the rack for 24–48h.

Special cases / safety notes:
- If host shows kernel oops / panic entries or if multiple GPUs show hardware errors, avoid driver-unload; prefer full host reboot.
- ipmitool commands may be unreliable if the BMC itself is under load; fall back to PDU-managed power-cycle.

Investigation action items (short-term):
- (Priya) Extract and correlate BMC fan and voltage telemetry for the affected rack for the full 72h window. Deadline: 2029-11-05.
- (Ethan) Run a controlled sustained-power kernel on a test node from same hardware batch with continuous monitoring of PMIC rails and nvlink state. Reproduce with progressive power draw. Deadline: 2029-11-08.
- (Maya) Open vendor support case, attach logs, ask for PMIC debug symbols and recommended firmware. JIRA ticket: JIRA-INC-8342 (assigned). Deadline: 2029-11-06.
- (Carlos) Prototype the "softquarantine" taint flow and alerting rule in staging; test detection rules for false positives. Deadline: 2029-11-04.

Longer-term mitigations (candidates):
- Fleet-level: add a mid-tier power-smoothing controller in the rack PDUs to reduce transient ripple under high-power transitions. (requires facilities / vendor collaboration).
- Driver-level: work with vendor to make NVML health probes non-blocking and resilient to transient PMIC events.
- Platform BIOS: test updated platform microcode that sequences PCIe devices more gracefully after device-level resets.
- Scheduling: add job-level annotations for sustained-power jobs and routing policies to distribute thermal/power load across racks.

Open questions and unknowns:
- Are PMIC events originating on GPU card PMICs or on the host PSU/VRM? (BMC / i2c traces should help).
- Why did two machines fail to auto-recover and require manual PDU cycle? Is the BMC starving or is a latch-up happening?
- Are there environmental correlations (AC mains fluctuation) that coincide with the cluster events? Coordinate with facilities.

Notes to self / nightshift observations (informal):
- I saw a synchronous fan oscillation on host-12 around +10s after the PMIC event — possible feedback loop between fan-controller and PMIC thermal logic.
- The jobs were dominated by long-run fp16 matmul kernels; scheduler currently treats GPU power demand as opaque. Short-term we should throttle scheduling of these jobs onto the same PSUs.
- One thought: implement a simple moving-window power-sum per-PDU and stop dispatching to a PDU when sustained > threshold. That avoids hardware changes short-term.

Appendices (quick link list):
- Commands I ran during triage:
  - journalctl -k -b --no-pager | sed -n '1,200p' > /tmp/dmesg-01.txt
  - tar czf /tmp/host-12-debug.tgz /var/log/nvidia* /var/log/messages /var/log/syslog /tmp/dmesg-01.txt
  - nvidia-smi dmon -s u -d 1 -o TSV > /tmp/nvmon-host12.tsv (used for short-run capture)
- Prom queries to reproduce panels:
  - rate(gpu_power_draw_watts[5m]) by (host)
  - increase(pcie_link_retrain_total[10m]) by (gpu_id, host)
  - gpu_fan_speed_rpm{host="host-12"}

Quick checkpoints for follow-ups:
- Confirm vendor acceptance of hardware ticket (Maya) -> expected 3–5d turnaround for debug.
- Controlled repro (Ethan) -> if we can reproduce, capture oscilloscope traces of VRM outputs.
- If repro fails, pivot to deeper driver instrumentation (non-blocking NVML wrappers).

If anything is unclear ping me in #sre-nightshift or DM. Leaving the doc in the drive so others can paste bits into Confluence runbook later.

-- Priya
